bullets.title: CPI Print at 8:30am Is the Day's Pivotal Macro Event — Hike vs. Hold Binary
bullets.body: Markets are pricing a 67% probability of a 25bp Fed hike at the Sep 16 FOMC, with options implying ~1% SPX move on the print. JPM forecasts headline CPI +0.38% m/m and core +0.21% m/m; a core rounded to 0.2% supports a hold (+0.5% to +1.25% SPX), while 0.3%+ triggers a hike and -1.5% to -2.5% SPX drawdown. Hedgeye's nowcast sits at 3.5% vs. street's 3.4% with further acceleration expected in Q4.

bullets.title: Fed Hike Fears Driving Bear Flattening — 10Y Approaching 5%, SPX P/E at Cycle Lows
bullets.body: 10Y Treasury yields reached highest since Oct 2023 at ~4.96%, with bear-flattening momentum and fair value argued near 5.8% if nominal GDP growth persists at 6.6%. VIX up 10%, stock-bond correlations rising, and SPX is at P/E levels seen at Iran War and Liberation Day lows. Capital Economics forecasts SPY bear market to 6,500 by end-2027 vs. 7,650 today.

bullets.title: Oil Pullback on Iran-Gulf Diplomacy Talks Provides Near-Term Relief
bullets.body: WTI fell ~3% to ~$99.58 and Brent pared gains on reports Gulf foreign ministers will meet Iranian counterparts Monday to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, diesel prices topped $6/gallon for the first time on record, crack spreads at all-time highs, and transport/warehousing services are up 12.9% YoY, feeding core inflation. Houthis also seized a key Yemeni port and struck Saudi oil infrastructure.

bullets.title: ECB Surprised Markets with Hawkish Hike; October Follow-On ~90% Priced
bullets.body: ECB raised rates to 2.50% with a hawkish tone, pushing markets to price ~90bps of additional tightening over the next year and ~80% probability of an October hike. Middle East escalation with Brent near $100/bbl vs. ECB's $90 assumption underpins the hawkish impulse; European gas consumption is down 20% since 2022-23, limiting energy shock tail risk but not inflation pressure.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Supercycle Unambiguous — Compute Tightening, Pricing Power Rising
bullets.body: Hyperscaler capex ramping ~30% YoY; MSFT plans to triple datacenter capacity to 38GW by 2032 (from ~12GW); bullish buyside consensus pencils AWS revenue growth at 50%+ in 2027 vs. Street's 34%. Older-generation GPU contracts are renewing at 20% premiums; OpenAI is rationing Pro subscriptions due to compute scarcity. Semi Analysis estimates $11.1T cumulative AI IT and datacenter capex by 2030, and Goldman notes realized equity correlations have fallen to 11, lowest in 25 years — historically a precursor to volatility spikes.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund Positioning Light but Re-Grossing; AI Exposure Near 2-Year Highs
bullets.body: Hedge fund gross exposure has risen over the past 5 days to the highest since late June (+1.3z), with net AI exposure rebounding near two-year highs. Light overall net positioning provides both downside cushion and upside accelerant if CPI is benign. CTA equity exposure sits at the 60th percentile with limited close sell triggers; Real Money inflows +$80B MTD via target-date funds.

bullets.title: SPX 7600 Is Key Gamma Pivot; Russell 2000 Flipping Bearish
bullets.body: SpotGamma identifies 7,600 as the negative gamma acceleration level for SPX; Hedgeye's risk range is 7,565–7,730 with resistance at 7,670. Russell 2000 changed to Bearish trend (most shorted at 92nd percentile) while Nasdaq remains Bullish (71st percentile short). Consumer discretionary is at the highest number of 52-week lows since April 2025.

bullets.title: Factor Rotation: US Quality/Momentum Sold Off Hard; Value Hedging, AI Names Resilient
bullets.body: JPM quant: US Quality and Momentum sold off -8.2% and -4.6% in August on hawkish Fed fears; Value held +0.6%. Globally, Asia ex-Japan Momentum surged +10.6%. 22V argues AI buildout names, Price Momentum, and EPS Momentum will outperform as economy slows, with rolling correlation between AI Buildout names and S&P Discretionary turning negative.

bullets.title: Hedgeye: Long Commodities/Energy, Short Growth/Bonds as Inflation Accelerates Into Q4
bullets.body: Hedgeye forecasts sticky inflation through December with no street consensus for the period; the 2Y Treasury yield is in a bullish trend making cycle highs. Recommended positioning: long inflation exposures (commodities, oil, energy, select international), short momentum, growth, bonds, and utilities. Russell 2000, growth stocks, industrials, retail, and China Tech are performing poorly.

bullets.title: Consumer Spending Re-Accelerated in August, But $20B Oil Headwind Looms into Year-End
bullets.body: JPM card data shows August consumer spending +5.1% YoY (vs. July +4.5%), with discretionary +5.4% YoY and a 2-year stack of +10.3% — strongest YTD. Strength was broad-based across income levels. However, ~$20B estimated gas-price headwind Sep–Dec (forecasting $4.45/gal avg) partially offsets $15B in tax refunds and $32B in COLA/Social Security tailwinds.

bullets.title: Nuclear Power Demand Accelerating From Datacenter Load; Supply Remains Inelastic
bullets.body: Hedgeye bullish on nuclear as data center power demand intensifies and Iran/Ukraine conflicts reduce global energy supply; grid replacement capacity is lagging aging infrastructure. An upcoming IPO wave (Westinghouse, Holtec) with government support underpins the CCJ bull case.

bullets.title: UK GDP Surges 0.4% in July, AI/Tech Driving; BoE Unlikely to Hike Near-Term
bullets.body: UK GDP printed +0.4% m/m in July vs. forecasts of 0.0%, led by IT/communications (+2.4% m/m) and computer programming services (+3.5% m/m). JPM raised 3Q annualized growth forecast to 2.0% from 0.8%. Household inflation expectations fell sharply to 3.2% (from 4.0%) on 1- and 2-year horizons, though wage settlement expectations remain sticky at ~3.6%.

bullets.title: Wedbush Reshuffles Cybersecurity Coverage: PANW/DDOG Up, CRWD/FTNT/CHKP Down
bullets.body: Wedbush raises PANW PT to $400 (+18% upside) and DDOG to $275 (+24%), while slashing CRWD PT from $720 to $250 (20% upside) and downgrading FTNT to Neutral ($155, 2% downside) and CHKP to Neutral. Jensen Huang separately highlighted cybersecurity as the next major AI opportunity.

bullets.title: Freight Market Bottoming; Transport Services CPI Up 12.9% YoY — Diesel at Record $6/Gallon
bullets.body: Conference takeaways from industrial names point to freight markets bottoming, with FDX, UPS, and CHRW showing improving pricing and operating leverage. August PPI for general freight trucking surged 13.9% YoY; diesel prices exceeded $6/gallon for the first time on record. Transport and warehousing services CPI running +12.9% YoY, leaking into core inflation.

bullets.title: GLP-1 Market: Lilly Tirzepatide Extends Share Lead to 56.9%; Oral Wegovy at 35% of Scripts
bullets.body: Lilly's tirzepatide holds 56.9% GLP-1 market share (up from 49.5% year ago), while Novo semaglutide is flat at 37.0%. Total GLP-1 Rx growth reaccelerated to +5.4% YoY as oral options broaden the market — oral Wegovy now represents 35% of total Wegovy scripts. Foundayo launched April 9 with 47.5K scripts.

bullets.title: Bridgewater: 14% of Jobs Could Be Radically Altered by AI in 3 Years; Regulation Lags
bullets.body: Bridgewater estimates 14% of jobs could be radically altered within 3 years as AI development continues to advance faster than regulatory frameworks. OpenAI is separately reported to be considering slowing cutting-edge AI development, with CEO Altman discussing the issue with staff.

bullets.title: Post-Election Seasonality Historically Bullish; Healthcare Best Sector in Midterm Periods
bullets.body: JPM notes that post-midterm SPX rallies have historically averaged +5.4% (3mo), +11.4% (6mo), and +14.7% (12mo) since 1990. If midterm seasonality takes hold, healthcare is typically the best performing sector. JPM maintains a Tactically Cautious/Neutral global equity stance ahead of today's CPI.

bullets.title: Copper Tariff No Longer Foregone Conclusion; Affordability Concerns Stalling Implementation
bullets.body: Reports suggest copper tariffs are stalling amid affordability concerns, removing a previously assumed headwind for EM commodity producers. Combined with a broader pullback in oil prices on Iran diplomacy, commodity-sensitive EM equity flows showed modest improvement with Brazil attracting $1.0B inflow.
